- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in following 7–14 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model may overcorrect; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% if sentiment turns negative.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if price is above 20-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 3+ swings in 7 days), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
